title: Parking the needle
subtitle: Where to leave the needle safely between stitches and colour changes.
excerpt: A loose needle left in the cloth leaves a rust mark or a permanent hole. Parking keeps it out of the way and off the furniture while you prepare the next thread.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. General needle care and safe storage during embroidery work.
Weldon's Practical Needlework, volume 1 (1886), Internet Archive. Workshop habits and needle safety.

glossaryTerms.definition: Any safe resting place for the needle when it is not in use: a needle minder magnet, a pin cushion, or a small piece of spare cloth kept alongside the main work.

content.text: Parking the needle means giving it a safe resting place when it is not being used. A needle left pushed into the main cloth leaves a ring mark or a permanent hole, especially on fine linen. A needle left loose on the arm of a sofa gets sat on.
Use a needle minder magnet: place one half on the front of the hoop or frame, the other behind. The magnet holds the needle on the front face of the cloth edge, not in the stitching area.
If using a pin cushion, push the needle fully in so the point is hidden. Keep the cushion within reach of the hoop.

In the border margin of the cloth, beyond where the design will be stitched, is an acceptable temporary park. Run the needle through the spare cloth parallel to the edge, not through the stitching ground.
Never park in the top-left corner of the stitching area. Your hand rests there when you turn the hoop and the needle goes into the palm.
Parking with a thread still on the needle

When working a colour-change method called needle parking, each colour stays on a dedicated needle. Once that colour finishes its stitches in a row, the needle is pushed to the front of the cloth and laid across the top of the hoop, with the thread hanging below. This keeps multiple threads in position for the next row without tangling or snipping. Each needle acts as its own

attrs.heading: What goes wrong
attrs.intro: Two habits that cause problems even though they feel harmless.

items.symptom: A ring mark appears on the cloth where the needle rested
items.cause: The needle was parked through the stitching ground for a long period, especially on linen, leaving a small hole that sets in the weave.
items.fix: Park in the cloth margin only. On linen, even a few hours is enough for a needle hole to become permanent. A needle minder is the safer default.

items.symptom: A needle is found weeks later under a cushion
items.cause: No dedicated parking place was set up beside the hoop.
items.fix: Fix the needle minder to the hoop before the first stitch. Make it a pre-session habit, like threading up.

content.text: Good parking practice matters most in long-session work and whenever children or pets are in the room. The
used for colour changes in counted-thread work is a technique in its own right, separate from general safe storage.
